handbook.powerfactor.arsenal.text:
All arsenal weapons run on FE: charge them in a Charger or on a Charging Pad.

Railgun: hold to charge. The view zooms and the reticle fills. Release to fire a hypersonic slug up to 160 blocks. It passes through every creature in line and punches through glass, leaves and ice. A full charge costs 12,000 FE.

Plasma Rifle: hold to stream plasma bolts that burst on impact without breaking blocks. Each shot heats the coils; at 100 the rifle vents for three seconds.

Singularity Launcher: consumes a Singularity and 250,000 FE. The black hole pulls every creature and loose item within 14 blocks for five seconds, harms anything at its horizon, then collapses in a blinding detonation. Terrain is safe unless the server enables super-weapon block damage.

Quantum Blade: an unbreakable energy sword. Right-click to phase-dash ten blocks, cutting everything you pass through.

Quantum Disassembler: pickaxe, axe, shovel and hoe in one. Sneak-use cycles Single, 3×3, 5×5 and Vein modes. The affected blocks are outlined, and drops go to your inventory.
handbook.powerfactor.arsenal.title: The Arsenal
handbook.powerfactor.black_hole.text:
The last word in power: a micro black hole held in a 5x5x5 containment sphere. The controller sits in the middle of the front of the bottom layer. The top and bottom layers are Containment Casing round a 3x3 of Field Coils; the four walls between are Event Horizon Glass with casing up the corners, an Accretion Injector in the middle of each wall's lower row and a Hawking Collector in the middle of the centre row of the side and back walls (the front's is a window). The 3x3x3 inside stays empty.

Load a Singularity into the hopper and press Ignite: 500M FE spins up a hole of mass 1,000. From then on it radiates (Hawking radiation grows as the hole shrinks: a quarter the mass, sixteen times the power) and evaporates, so it must be fed: any item is one unit of mass, Exotic Matter a hundred, a Singularity a thousand. Matter falling in shines as accretion. Holding it costs a containment field that grows with its size.

Auto feeds the hole to hold a target mass. The curve on the console shows the bargain: at 1,000 it nets about 1.3M FE/t on 1.4 items a second; at 200, 36M FE/t, but on 36 items a second, and if the feed stops it is gone in seconds, in a burst. Let the stored energy run below what the field needs and the hole escapes as a wandering singularity.
handbook.powerfactor.black_hole.title: Black Hole Power Plant
handbook.powerfactor.chargers.text:
The Wireless Charger tops up the FE gear of every player within 16 blocks (8 more per Range Upgrade, up to 40): power armour, tools, weapons, anything with an energy store, up to 8,000 FE/t shared. Arcs of power reach out to whoever it's charging.

The Dimensional Wireless Charger charges the players bound to it (right-click to bind or unbind) wherever they are, in any dimension, at up to 40,000 FE/t. A quarter is lost crossing between worlds. A pillar of light rises from it while it sends.
handbook.powerfactor.chargers.title: Wireless Charging
handbook.powerfactor.chips.text:
Electronics start as silicon. Roll silicon into wafers in the Rolling Mill. The Laser Engraver patterns a wafer through a photomask: the mask in its tool slot decides the chip. It isn't used up, but every die wears it a little.

Logic mask + 2 gold nuggets: Microprocessor. Memory mask + 2 redstone: 2 Memory Chips. Power mask + copper dust: 2 Power Transistors. Sensor mask + quartz: Sensor Chip.

Advanced Circuits now need a microprocessor and memory on a printed circuit board. VFD upgrades use power transistors, the clamp meter a sensor chip, the Upgrade Table a microprocessor.
handbook.powerfactor.chips.title: Chips
handbook.powerfactor.devices.text:
Tesla Coil: charges a capacitor from the grid, then throws lightning at the nearest hostile mob it can see within 14 blocks, arcing on to a second one. It never targets players. Each strike costs 2,500 FE and is a sharp reactive pulse on the grid, so give it a strong grid or a capacitor bank nearby, or the lights will flicker.

LED Grow Lamp: hang it above crops. It lights them, so they grow underground, and gives every plant in a 9x9 area up to six blocks below many extra growth ticks: several times faster farms for 24 FE/t.
handbook.powerfactor.devices.title: Tesla Coil & Grow Lamp
handbook.powerfactor.drones.text: The Drone Hub's AI surveys the ground in a 49-block-wide column under and around it, clusters the ore it finds into veins and scores each one: what the ore is worth, how big the vein is, how far away, and whether it touches lava. Put up to four Mining Drones in its bay and it sends each to the best unclaimed vein. The drones fly out (phasing through stone in a bore field), cut each ore block with a laser, and fly the haul home; the hub's console maps the veins and drones live and keeps a log of every decision the AI makes. Each launch charges a drone's 30,000 FE battery; Speed cards make them fly faster. Re-surveys every two minutes.
handbook.powerfactor.drones.title: AI Mining Drones
handbook.powerfactor.ender.text:
Ender Transmitters turn FE into an EE carrier and beam it to Ender Receivers on the same channel, even across dimensions. The receiver rectifies it back to FE at 85%.

There's a catch. Sending makes the transmitter a big reactive load on its own grid, and busy links radiate interference: every grid within about 48 blocks sees flickering voltage and jittering frequency, so motors slow and trip. Keep wireless away from your factory, or support those grids with capacitors and condensers.
handbook.powerfactor.ender.title: Ender Energy
handbook.powerfactor.exotic.text:
Four fictional materials lie beyond iron and diamond. All use common c: tags, so other mods can use them.

Adamantium: very rare, deep in deepslate (y -64 to -36), never touching caves. Arc-smelt raw adamantium with graphite. Adamantium pickaxes and shovels excavate 3×3.

Faradaenium: glowing teal veins in End stone. Blast or smelt it. Faradaenium tools are magnetic, and the sword chains lightning.

Cortanium: one nearly indestructible crimson block in roughly every sixteen chunks, between y -60 and -48. Arc-smelt four shards with netherite scrap. Cortanium tools never break and fell whole veins and trees.

Qubit Crystal: violet crystals deep underground, the root of the quantum chain. Crush crystals into Quantum Dust. Alloy dust with adamantium into Quantum Alloy. Laser-engrave crystals and an ender pearl into an Entangled Pair, then engrave that onto a microprocessor to make a Quantum Processor. Quantum Alloy tools do everything at once: 5×5 excavation, vein mining, magnetism and an unbreakable rift-tearing blade.

Sneak to mine single blocks. Each ore can be disabled in the server config's worldgen section.

Armor: each material makes a full suit. Wearing all four pieces of one material grants its set bonus. Adamantium Bulwark gives resistance. Faradaenium Dynamo gives speed and arcs lightning into attackers. Cortanium Crucible never breaks, grants fire immunity and strength, and sets attackers alight. Quantum Phase does all of that, adds night vision and removes fall damage, and a phase shift lets one blow pass through you every eight seconds.

Meteors: on some nights a meteor streaks down within a few dozen blocks of you. Its crater holds a core of Meteorite studded with exotic ore. Crush Meteorite for raw iron and a chance of adamantium, faradaenium, qubit crystal or cortanium. Servers can turn meteors or their craters off in the config.
handbook.powerfactor.exotic.title: Exotic Ores & Tools
handbook.powerfactor.farming.text: The Farm Gantry runs an overhead crane over the 9x9 field in front of it. Watch the bridge roll down the rails and the carriage cross it, square by square: the tool head drops to till dirt and grass into farmland, plant seeds from its seed slots, and cut ripe crops (and melons and pumpkins off their stems). It keeps a seed from each harvest to replant and sends the rest to its harvest slots, ready for pipes. Pipe water into it and it irrigates every square it passes, so the field never dries. 60 FE per job and 10 FE/t while moving.
handbook.powerfactor.farming.title: Farm Gantry
handbook.powerfactor.fission.text:
Mine uranium deep underground and smelt it into ingots. An Isotope Centrifuge separates nine ingots into one Enriched Uranium and eight Depleted; three enriched make a Uranium Fuel Rod.

Build the reactor as a box, 5 to 18 blocks on each side, framed in Reactor Casing along every edge and corner; the walls between can be Casing or Reactor Glass, so you can glaze every face. Reactor Ports and Logic Adapters go in the walls (not the edges), and the controller in one wall. Inside, stand columns of Fuel Assemblies from floor to roof, each with a Control Rod Drive above it in the roof, and fill the rest with water, which moderates and cools (or with Graphite Moderator). Each assembly holds one rod.

In water a running core glows Cherenkov blue: a shimmering sheath round every fuel column, light rippling over the glass, and a blue flash when the power surges. The fuel lights the room more brightly as power rises, and a hot core boils streams of bubbles. Fuel in graphite makes no blue light; it glows red with heat instead. Glass lets gamma out as well as light: stand close to a glass reactor at power and the Geiger counter climbs and your view speckles. Casing and the pool stop it.

Ports switch between Coolant (pipe coolant in and steam or hot coolant out) and Fuel (rods in, spent rods out).

Coolant: plain water boils into steam right in the core, and its steam voids hold the power down. Three loop coolants stay liquid and come out hot instead: pipe them through a Heat Exchanger, which boils water into steam and sends the coolant back cold. Heavy Water (spun out of a water bucket in the centrifuge) moderates better and makes fuel last a third longer. Liquid Sodium (soda ash from smelted dried kelp, reduced with coal) takes heat three times as well, so the core runs far denser, but losing sodium adds reactivity. Molten Salt (soda ash, blaze powder and amethyst) takes heat twice as well and lets the fuel run 400 K hotter. The coolant tank holds one kind at a time: Purge it on the console (shut down and cool) to change.

On the console, pull the rods out slowly until the period settles, or set a target and press Auto. Watch the temperature: hot fuel brakes itself, but run it dry or yank the rods and it melts down. After a shutdown from high power, xenon builds and holds the core down for a while (the iodine pit). The interlocks scram it at the trip setpoints; a Logic Adapter outputs any alarm as redstone, and a redstone signal into one SCRAMs the reactor.

A reactor makes far more steam than ordinary turbines can take. Build a High-Pressure Turbine: 5 wide, 3 tall and 9 long, Turbine Casing all round with fifteen Steam Rotors and six Generator Magnets inside, the controller in the middle of the front. It turns 2,500 mB of steam a tick into 50,000 FE/t.

Spent rods are fiercely radioactive: carry them only in a full Hazmat Suit. A Geiger Counter clicks and reads the dose rate where you stand; a Dosimeter keeps the dose you have taken in all. The centrifuge reprocesses them into Plutonium, Depleted Uranium and Nuclear Waste; plutonium and depleted uranium make mox rods.
handbook.powerfactor.fission.title: Fission Reactor
handbook.powerfactor.fusion.text:
A 5×5×3 tokamak. Sneak-use the controller with materials in your inventory to build it automatically.

Bottom layer: 25 Fusion Shielding. Middle: a ring of Toroidal Field Magnets with the controller in the front middle and a hollow 3×3 chamber inside. Top: Shielding around a 3×3 Fusion Viewport.

Pipe hydrogen (from Electrolyzers) into any casing and feed it FE. With 1,000 mB of hydrogen stored, the reactor pours a 50M FE ignition pulse into the plasma. At ignition it burns up to 8 mB of hydrogen a tick (two Electrolyzers keep it fed) and delivers up to 250,000 FE/t through the controller and every casing. If the hydrogen runs dry, the plasma cools and quenches, and you have to ignite it again.
handbook.powerfactor.fusion.title: Fusion Reactor
handbook.powerfactor.generators.text:
Coal Turbine and Diesel Generator: synchronous, so they supply EE. The diesel starts in two seconds and burns modded diesel or fuel, or lava at a worse rate. Hydro Turbine: flowing water around it; also synchronous. Solar Panel and Wind Turbine: FE only.

Wind Turbine: stack Wind Turbine Tower sections (they taper as they rise) and put the turbine on top. The 13-block rotor needs clear air in front, so build at least 6 sections high; taller towers catch stronger wind. It starts at 3 m/s, reaches full output at 12 m/s and pitches its blades to hold it there. Above 25 m/s, in a storm, it feathers and brakes until the wind drops. Cable it at the foot of the tower.

Synchronous Condenser: a spinning machine that only makes EE. Battery Bank: stores 2M FE. Generation serves machines first; the bank supplies remaining demand, including on a cold or rebuilt grid. Idle and full networks do not drain it. Multiple banks share backup duty within the wire's rating, including line losses.

Steam power: form a 3x3x3 Steam Boiler with 23 Boiler Casings, one Firebox and two Steam Drums. Feed cold water and furnace fuel through its controller or formed ports. Once hot it produces up to 80 mB/t of steam. Steam Pipes carry only steam, up to 4000 mB per extraction every ten ticks; sneak-use an endpoint to extract, as with fluid pipes. The 3x2x5 Steam Turbine needs 26 Turbine Casings, two Steam Rotors and a Generator Magnet. It synchronizes over ten seconds and generates up to 800 FE/t, with EE support. Use the hologram or sneak-use assembly for either structure. Hot condensate must leave the turbine: pipe it through a powered Cooling Tower, then return its cold water to the boiler. Cooling towers need an open vent to the sky. Steam pipes and turbines accept c:steam from other mods; cooling towers accept c:hot_water. The boiler pauses its burner at 60% pressure and resumes at 40%; blocked outlets hold safely. Dry firing can trip it: supply water and let it cool.

Geothermal Generator: any adjacent lava gives 64 FE/t; magma gives 24. Thermoelectric Generator: put a hot source and water or ice on opposite faces, for up to 48 FE/t. A Rain Collector catches 2 mB/t of actual rain, or 6 during thunderstorms, without FE. A roof stops collection. Pipe its water into your boiler to replenish the loop.
handbook.powerfactor.generators.title: Generators & Storage
handbook.powerfactor.grid.text:
Connected wire of one kind forms a grid, solved every tick like a real AC bus.

Voltage sags as the grid loads up, and EE sags it three times harder than FE. Line loss goes with current squared, and current follows CE, so a poor power factor wastes FE as heat in the wires.

Turbines set the frequency and droop slightly under load (60 Hz down to about 58). They also supply the grid's EE. Solar, wind and batteries can't, so a grid of those plus motors needs capacitors or a synchronous condenser.
handbook.powerfactor.grid.title: Wires and Grids
handbook.powerfactor.hydrogen.text:
Wind blows when it likes. Store it as hydrogen.

The Electrolyzer splits water into hydrogen with grid power (100 FE per 4 mB). Pipe water in and hydrogen out to a Fluid Tank, where it shows as a gas that thickens with pressure.

The Hydrogen Fuel Cell turns it back into FE (about 11 FE per mB, so roughly 45% round trip, like real systems). Its inverter is grid-forming: it sets 60 Hz and supplies EE like a synchronous generator, so wind plus hydrogen can run a whole grid with nothing spinning. The fuel cell also accepts other mods' fluids tagged c:hydrogen.
handbook.powerfactor.hydrogen.title: Hydrogen
handbook.powerfactor.logistics.text:
Item Pipes and Fluid Pipes link up automatically. Arms into inventories insert by default. Right-click an arm with an empty hand to make it extract (orange rings); right-click again to disable it.

Fluid Tanks hold 32 buckets and keep their contents when broken. The Electric Pump draws water from a source block below it without using it up.

Sneak-use a pipe with an empty hand to open Pipe Routing. Each world-direction face has four ghost references, an allow/block mode, exact component matching and destination priority. Filled containers select fluid references. High priorities fill first; full targets overflow to lower priorities. Filters affect endpoints, while pipe-to-pipe links pass through. Breaking or wrench-packing a pipe preserves its routing settings.
handbook.powerfactor.logistics.title: Pipes and Tanks
handbook.powerfactor.machines.text:
Crusher: ore to two dusts, plus gravel, sand and more. Electric Furnace: smelts 25% faster on resistive elements, PF 1.0. Alloy Furnace: induction heating (PF 0.6), makes brass, bronze, electrum and rubber. Arc Furnace: steel, aluminum, silicon and graphite; it needs graphite electrodes and its arc makes the grid flicker. Wire Drawer, Rolling Mill: fine wire and plates. Ore Washer: three dusts per ore with water.

Motor-driven machines slow down on low voltage or frequency and trip below 0.75 pu.

Mechanical Press: fit a Plate Press Die for ingots to plates, or a Gear Press Die for four ingots to a gear. Dies wear once per job and last 512 jobs. Mixer: copper and zinc dust to brass, copper and tin to bronze, or gold and silver to electrum; smelt the blended dust into ingots. Centrifuge: four dirt to a clay ball and sand, or four gravel to flint and two sand. Sawmill: a log to six planks and a stick. All four accept upgrades and side configuration, and support automatic input and output.

Early workshop: craft a Forge Hammer and Wire Cutters from iron and sticks. Two ingots plus a hammer make one plate; a plate plus cutters makes two wires. Both tools return to the grid and wear once per operation. Machines improve material yield: the Rolling Mill or Mechanical Press makes a plate from one ingot, and the Wire Drawer makes three fine wires from one ingot. Heat four coal dust in the Alloy Furnace to make starting graphite for electrodes. The first Arc Furnace uses iron plates and a control circuit, so its own steel and silicon are not needed to build it.

Mix a slimeball, clay ball and coal or charcoal to make two rubber. Natural latex remains renewable. Rubber from other mods can substitute in tagged insulation recipes. Wind turbines now need three blades, two motors, a generator magnet, two steel blocks and an advanced circuit; tower sections craft in pairs.
handbook.powerfactor.machines.title: Machines
handbook.powerfactor.mobs.text:
Use a Soul Snare on a mob to take an imprint of its kind; the mob is unharmed. Put the filled snare in a Spawner Cage and you'll see the mob turning inside the bars, soul fire rising round it until a copy steps out two blocks in front. Each copy costs 2,000 FE plus 400 per point of the mob's health, and the cage waits while eight of them crowd the space. Speed and Efficiency cards apply. Bosses can't be snared.

Point a Mob Grinder at the same space. Its saw spins up and cuts down anything in the 5x3x5 zone in front of it as a player would, so rare drops and experience fall. It gathers the drops into its grid and the experience into a store you draw from its console. Named mobs and pets are spared.
handbook.powerfactor.mobs.title: Mob Farming
handbook.powerfactor.oil.text:
Crude oil lies in reservoirs deep underground, and sometimes seeps up as tar pits in deserts and badlands. Build a Pumpjack above a 3x3 layer of nine Pumpjack Foundation blocks, over a reservoir (it searches straight down, then up to 8 blocks sideways): the nodding donkey lifts 25 mB of crude per tick for 60 FE/t until the reservoir runs dry.

Pipe the crude to an Oil Refinery, a multiblock: the controller sits front-centre of a 3x3 base of Refinery Casing, with three Distillation Column blocks stacked on the middle casing; a hologram shows what's missing. Sneak-use the controller with an empty hand or a structure part to build from inventory. The wind turbine can build its six tower sections the same way. Clear the hologram first; assembly never replaces obstructions. Cables and pipes attach to any casing. The distillation column splits 10 mB of crude into 5 mB of diesel and 4 mB of jet fuel every tick (100 FE/t). Diesel runs the Diesel Generator; jet fuel is available for future aircraft. Buckets work for all three. The refinery accepts other mods' fluids tagged c:crude_oil.
handbook.powerfactor.oil.title: Oil
handbook.powerfactor.ores.text:
New ores: zinc, tin, lead, silver and bauxite (aluminum). Each can be turned off in the common config if another mod provides it. PowerFactor uses the shared c: tags, so other mods' ores work in every machine.

Smelting gives one ingot per ore, the crusher two dusts, and the ore washer three. Alloys: brass (3 copper + zinc), bronze (3 copper + tin), electrum (gold + silver). Steel and aluminum come from the arc furnace.

Rubber trees grow in jungles, swamps and forests. Tap weeping logs with a Tree Tap for latex, then smelt or alloy it into rubber.

Factory construction: Steel Beams form columns and girders (place against a face to choose their axis). Steel Catwalks are thin grated floors. Riveted Steel, Hazard Blocks and Warning Blocks finish walls and mark dangerous machinery. Find their crafting recipes in JEI.
handbook.powerfactor.ores.title: Ores and Materials
handbook.powerfactor.pocket.text:
A Dimensional Pocket is bigger on the inside. Use it to step into a private room, 7 blocks across, in a dimension of its own; use any wall panel to step back out beside the door. Break the pocket and the room goes with it, contents and all, wherever you place it next. Use a Spatial Expander on it to grow the room to 13 and then 21 blocks across; what's inside stays put.

The room stays loaded while its door is, so machines inside keep running. Place a Pocket Port inside, against a machine or chest, and anything piped into the pocket outside (items, fluids or energy) goes to it, and can be pulled back out.
handbook.powerfactor.pocket.title: Pocket Dimensions
handbook.powerfactor.pocket_void.text:
Bedrock can't be broken, but it can be chipped. Set off TNT right against it and a Bedrock Fragment may fly off (the closer the blast, the better the odds; two at most a blast). Four fragments and a glowstone dust make two Essence of Bedrock.

A Pocket Void is a pouch held open on nothing by that essence: nine slots, each holding one kind of item by the thousand. Use it to open it. Click a cell to take a stack or put what you carry; right-click for half or one; shift-click to send a stack to your inventory; ctrl-click to lock a cell to its kind; alt- or middle-click to choose the cell it builds with when you use it on a block. Its pickup mode pulls in matching items, anything, or matching items with the excess deleted (cobblestone, dirt). A Void Core turns it into a Deep Pocket Void, everything inside kept.

Lightning fuses sand: a bolt landing on sand (a lightning rod standing in it works) turns some into Fused Sand, which breaks into Fulgurite.

Elevators: stand on one and jump to rise to the next of the same colour above, sneak to drop to the one below, up to 32 blocks with two clear blocks over the landing. Dye them to run separate shafts side by side. A Chunk Loader Card in any machine's upgrade slots keeps that machine's chunk loaded.
handbook.powerfactor.pocket_void.title: Bedrock and the Pocket Void
handbook.powerfactor.power_factor.text:
Motors draw EE, and lightly loaded motors draw it worst: a crusher idling between jobs runs at about PF 0.25.

Capacitor Banks supply EE locally so the generator doesn't have to, which brings voltage back up and cuts losses. Their output goes with V^2, and too many push the grid to a leading PF and raise the voltage. Above 1.12 pu they trip out.

The Automatic Capacitor Bank switches six 20 EE steps in and out every two seconds to hold the grid near PF 1.0. Watch its cans light up.
handbook.powerfactor.power_factor.title: PF Correction
handbook.powerfactor.power_net.text:
A power network moves FE without wires, any distance and between dimensions. Every network needs one Power Net Controller. Power Plugs take power from whatever touches them (generators, batteries, cables) and Power Points give it to whatever touches them; Power Cells store it (4M, 64M and 1G FE).

Open any device to choose or create a network: name it, pick its colour (the devices glow in it) and say who may use it: Public, Private (you and the people you add) or Password. Each device has a name, a priority (higher is served first, and Cells give up their charge from the lowest), a transfer limit (800,000 FE/t by default, or none), Surge (always served first) and can keep its own chunk loaded. The Links tab lists every device with its flow; Stats graphs the last minute; People adds members and admins and sets the controller's wireless charging of members' hotbar, armour, offhand and pack.

Plugs and Points are made from Fulgurite (sand fused by lightning). A Net Configurator copies a device's settings (sneak-use) and pastes them on another (use). New devices you place join the network you last used.
handbook.powerfactor.power_net.title: Wireless Power Networks
handbook.powerfactor.power_tools.text:
Electric Chainsaw: an axe on FE. Cut one log of a tree and the whole tree comes down, and its leaves drop their saplings soon after. Sneak to cut a single log. It only fells real trees (logs with natural leaves), so your log cabin is safe.

Electric Jetpack: wear it in the chest slot. Hold Jump to climb; press J by default to toggle hover, which holds you in the air while you build. Sneak to sink. Thrust costs 50 FE/t, hover 18.

Clamp Meter: hold it and look at any wire or machine for a live reading of voltage, frequency, FE, EE, CE and power factor, with a phasor diagram.

Induction Charging Pad: stand on it and everything you carry charges.

Power Armor: helmet, chest plate, exoskeleton leggings and boots have individual FE batteries. Charge them in a Charger or by standing on a powered Charging Pad. The hull supplies iron-level armor without power. Each charged piece shields 8% of damage remaining after armor, paying 120 FE per point absorbed; Plating adds 2% per module, capped at 50% for the suit. Leg servos add 25% movement speed, higher jumps and one-block steps. Speed modules add 15% each; Jump Servo modules add height. Sneak or disable movement assists to move normally. Boots spend FE to cushion five blocks of a fall beyond the safe distance; Shock Absorbers add three blocks each. Empty batteries stop powered abilities. Open suit settings with B to see batteries and toggle movement assists, night vision or jetpack hover.

Put a chest plate in the Upgrade Table and fit an actual Electric Jetpack into a socket. It remains removable with its stored charge and upgrades; flight uses the chest battery. Thruster and Efficiency modules in the chest and fitted jetpack combine up to the usual three-module limit. Hold Jump to climb, J toggles hover by default and Sneak descends. All armor takes Battery, Efficiency and Plating modules. Helmets also take Night Vision and Rebreather modules for powered vision and underwater air. The helmet utilities, locomotion, landing cushion and shield all consume FE; keep an eye on the four-battery HUD.

Movement kit: the Powered Grapple has a 64-block cable and 120,000 FE battery. G casts or retracts from your inventory; right-click works when held. The hook attaches to solid terrain or a moving entity. It reels you toward the anchor for 12 FE/t; hold Sneak to stop the reel and swing on a fixed cable. Jump releases without killing momentum. Broken anchors, obstructed cables, excessive range, empty batteries or dropping the device release the hook. Fit Battery, Efficiency or Speed modules in the Upgrade Table to improve the grapple.

A Wingsuit can be worn directly or fitted into a Power Chestplate socket alongside a jetpack. Press U in the air to deploy or fold. W/S pitch down/up and A/D bank; mouse look also sets heading. Dive for speed, then pull up to trade momentum for altitude. Sneak airbrakes. Low airspeed stalls: the wingsuit needs altitude and momentum. Release a swinging or reeling grapple into a glide to keep your speed. A fitted jetpack can regain altitude: Jump folds the wingsuit and resumes thrust. Wingsuit fabric folds smoothly, stretches between the arms and hips, and has a leg membrane. Its gliding pose, camera bank and wind sound follow motion. The suit screen controls both flight modes, and the movement HUD shows cable mode, charge, distance and airspeed.

The Electric Rover is a fast single-seat off-road vehicle with a 500,000 FE battery. Place it on clear ground and right-click to sit. W/S accelerate and reverse, A/D steer, Jump brakes and Sprint boosts. Sneak exits. It climbs one-block steps using collision handling, and brakes automatically if the driver leaves or input stops. Drive uses 20 FE/t, boost 50 FE/t. Empty batteries coast but cannot accelerate. Park above a powered Charging Pad to recharge; the packed vehicle also charges as an FE item. Sneak-use a wrench on a stopped, empty rover to pack it without losing battery or hull state. Steel ingots repair 10 HP each. The chassis has 80 HP; a destroyed rover becomes scrap.
handbook.powerfactor.power_tools.title: Power Tools
handbook.powerfactor.processing.text:
Every step up the ore ladder pays more metal per ore.

Crusher: 2 dust. Ore Washer: 3 dust with water.

Wash Plant (4x): a placer-mine wash line you build: the Wash Plant shaker table at the front, a six-block Sluice Box line running back on Wash Plant Frame legs, three Trommel sections over its back half and a Feed Hopper on a frame column at the end. Sneak-use the table to see the hologram or build it from your inventory. Pipe in water (1,000 mB a load) and 400 FE/t; feed raw ore or ore blocks into the hopper or the table. Each load becomes four concentrate, each of which smelts to an ingot, with the heavies a sluice catches: gold nuggets, flint, lapis and the odd diamond or emerald. Gravel and sand pan out gold.

Chemistry (4x, 5x): spin sulfur out of coal or netherrack in a Centrifuge. The Chemical Reactor burns it with hydrogen from an Electrolyser and absorbs it in water to make sulfuric acid. The Ore Dissolver leaches raw ore in acid and grows four crystals; a Quantum Catalyst in its catalyst slot makes it five. Crystals crush to dust.
handbook.powerfactor.processing.title: Ore Processing
handbook.powerfactor.quantum.text:
Particle Collider: accelerates matter around a superconducting ring until it banks the collision energy (up to 250,000 FE/t). Diamond becomes two Qubit Crystals (4M FE). Two Ender Pearls become Raw Faradaenium (8M FE). Eight Iron Ingots become Raw Adamantium (16M FE). Netherite Scrap becomes a Cortanium Shard (30M FE). Four Qubit Crystals become Exotic Matter (25M FE), and four Exotic Matter become a Singularity (80M FE). Three Wither Skeleton Skulls become a Nether Star.

Zero-Point Energy Generator: Exotic Matter holds a pocket of false vacuum open. The generator takes thirty seconds to stabilise, then supplies up to 50,000 FE/t to every adjacent receiver. One Exotic Matter lasts twenty minutes. Arcs strike its electrodes, and the gyroscope spins faster as the vacuum stabilises.

Quantum Crafting Processors, Quantum Storage Cells, the Quantum Quarry, Quantum Wireless Terminal and Quantum Data Cable all use Quantum Processors and Quantum Alloy.

Quantum Teleporter: entangle two pads by using an Entangled Qubit Pair on one, then on the other (the pair is used up). Stand still on a linked, powered pad for a moment-and-a-half to jump to its partner, in any dimension. A jump costs 5,000 FE plus 20 FE per block of distance, or 500,000 FE between dimensions. Step off the arrival pad before jumping back.

Abandoned labs: rare sealed rooms deep in the deepslate hold a dead collider, qubit crystal growing through the walls, a rift that still leaks endermites, and the last researcher's chest. Servers can turn them off in the worldgen config.

Robot Arm: place it facing the inventory to deliver to; it reaches into the inventory behind it, swings round and sets stacks of up to 16 down in front, using 250 FE a move. Use the arm with an item to move only that item; sneak-use with an empty hand to clear the filter.

Orbital Collector: give it open sky and power. At night it tracks the heavens and pulls drifting matter down a collection beam. Each minute-long pass costs 3M FE and yields Cosmic Dust (nine fuse into Exotic Matter), often qubit crystal or raw faradaenium, sometimes Meteorite, and very rarely a Nether Star.

Hover-Bike: a repulsor bike that rides a cushion a block above land or water. W/S throttle, A/D steer (it banks into turns), Sprint boosts, and Jump lifts it over obstacles. It runs on a 1M FE battery; park it over a Charging Pad to top up, and sneak-use a wrench to pack it into an item, charge and hull intact.

Gravity Lift: a pad that projects a field column straight up to the first solid block (up to 24). Step in to float up; sneak to sink gently. Nobody takes fall damage inside it. Items ride it too. 20 FE per entity carried each tick.

Logic Controller: a small programmable redstone controller. Inputs on its left, back and right; output from its front. Programs: AND, OR, XOR, NAND, set/reset latch, timer (pulses every N ticks while back is on), delay (back input N ticks later) and count (a pulse after every N back-input pulses). Its console shows live lamps and a logic trace.

Mech Suit: a three-block walker you climb into. W/S walks, A/D turns, Sprint runs, Jump fires the jump-jets; it steps up 1.5 blocks, and a landing from more than three blocks slams a shockwave into nearby creatures. 2M FE battery (Charging Pads reach it); repair with steel; sneak-use a wrench to pack it up.

Space Elevator: the capstone. Place the anchor under open sky, power it and feed it Nanotube Tether Segments; it raises one every three seconds (50,000 FE each). With all 64 up, the orbital station beams down 120,000 FE/t of space solar power, day and night, into every adjacent receiver. Sneak-use the finished anchor to ride the climber up the tether; you drift home on slow fall.
handbook.powerfactor.quantum.title: Quantum Machines
handbook.powerfactor.quarry.text:
Quarries dig a square in front of them, layer by layer, down to just above the world floor. Products go into a touching storage network (via any network block next to the quarry) or any adjacent inventory; when nothing has room the quarry waits.

The Industrial Quarry drives a laser gantry over squares of 9 to 33 blocks, one block every four ticks. The Quantum Quarry needs no frame. It folds space under a floating projector, reaches 65×65, takes four blocks a tick and costs 40% less per block. Speed cards double the rate each.

Energy per block: 25 FE × hardness, ×1.585 per Fortune level, ×4 with Silk Touch. Fluids are cleared, and blocks with block entities (chests, spawners, machines) are left alone. Void mode discards rubble so storage fills only with ores and gems.
handbook.powerfactor.quarry.title: Quarries
handbook.powerfactor.radio.text: Walkie-talkies use your real microphone through the Simple Voice Chat mod. Hold one and talk: everyone carrying a switched-on walkie-talkie on the same channel hears you through its little speaker, with more static the further away they are, out to about 190 blocks. Use the walkie-talkie to change channel (1-16); sneak-use to switch it off. Talking uses a little charge; charge it in a charger.\n\nRadio Towers relay calls: when both people are within about 96 blocks of a powered tower, they can talk at any distance, crystal clear. A blackout takes the towers off the air.
handbook.powerfactor.radio.title: Radio
handbook.powerfactor.redstone.text:
Red Alloy Wire (copper and redstone) carries a signal at full strength along its whole run, however long, climbs blocks like redstone and powers what it points at and the block under it. Insulated Wire, in sixteen colours, joins only its own colour and red alloy and doesn't power the block it lies on, so colours can run side by side. Bundled Cable carries all sixteen colours at once: run insulated wires into it at one end and out of it at the other.

Gates sit on stone circuit plates: inputs on the left, back and right, output at the front, and a lamp shows each. AND, OR, not, NAND, nor, XOR, xnor, Buffer, Multiplexer, Pulse Former, Repeater, Randomizer, rs Latch, Toggle Latch, Timer and Counter. A Screwdriver turns a gate; sneak-use it to choose which inputs a logic gate reads. Use a Repeater or Timer bare-handed to step its delay (sneak for back), and a Counter to set its target.

Illumar Lamps come in sixteen colours and glow with a soft halo when powered; Inverted lamps are lit until powered. The wireless antennas carry any signal between them on a dye channel, any distance.
handbook.powerfactor.redstone.title: Red Alloy, Gates and Lamps
handbook.powerfactor.scada.text:
SCADA is the control room. Run Fiber Optic Cable from a SCADA Terminal to your machines: it lists every device live with on/off switches, system totals and 60-second frequency and voltage trends. Alarms sound on faults.

SCADA Displays placed side by side form one wall screen that lays itself out by size, from a single readout up to a full HMI with an automatic one-line diagram of your grid. Connect any panel to fiber; right-click to change page.
handbook.powerfactor.scada.title: SCADA
handbook.powerfactor.starforge.text:
Paxels (pickaxe, axe, shovel and hoe in one) cannot be crafted. They are fused in the Starforge, a 3×3×3 structure:

Bottom layer: the Starforge controller front-centre, a Block of Adamantium in the middle, Starforge Frames all around.
Middle layer: four Starforge Pylons at the corners and the Starforge Crucible in the centre.
Top layer: Starforge Frames with a Block of Qubit Crystal in the centre as the focusing lens.

Holograms show missing parts; sneak-use the controller with the materials in your inventory to auto-build.

Load a pickaxe, axe and shovel of one material plus its catalyst. The catalyst is a Diamond Block, Netherite Block, or Block of Adamantium, Faradaenium or Cortanium; Quantum tools take a Singularity. The forge draws up to 400,000 FE/t and needs 10M FE (diamond) to 200M FE (quantum). The paxel keeps the best enchantments from all three tools, and exotic paxels keep their material's abilities.
handbook.powerfactor.starforge.title: The Starforge & Paxels
handbook.powerfactor.start.text:
Welcome to PowerFactor: AC power the way real grids work.

Build a Coal Turbine (iron, copper coils, turbine blades, a furnace) and feed it coal. It takes about ten seconds to spin up to 3,600 RPM. Its breaker closes at 57 Hz and it starts pushing FE out of every face except the front. Run Copper Wire from it to your machines.

Right-click any machine for its GUI. The tabs on the right edge hold the Electrical analyzer, Upgrades and Configuration.
handbook.powerfactor.start.title: Getting Started
handbook.powerfactor.storage.text:
A Storage Controller powers a network of Data Cables. Feed it FE from your grid; every device draws a little power, shown as the controller's load. Drive Bays hold Storage Cells (1k to Quantum). Each cell stores 8 items per byte and reserves bytes for every distinct item type. Storage Buses turn an adjacent chest or any inventory into network storage; priority decides where items go.

Terminals show everything on the network. Left-click takes a stack, right-click half, Shift-click sends it to your inventory; click with an item to store it. Search with words, @mod or #tag. The Crafting Terminal refills its grid from the network.

Autocrafting: encode Crafting Patterns in the Pattern Terminal and put them in a Molecular Assembler; encode Processing Patterns and put them in a Pattern Provider next to a machine. The provider pushes inputs into the machine; set the machine to eject its products back into the provider. Add a Crafting Processor, then Ctrl-click a craftable item to plan and start a craft. Quantum Crafting Processors run four jobs at once.

Fluids: Fluid Cells (4k, 64k, Quantum) go in Drive Bays beside item cells; each byte holds eight buckets. Pipes can push fluid into the Storage Controller and pull it back out. The Fluid Terminal lists every fluid: click a fluid with an empty bucket or tank to fill it, or click with a full one to pour it in.

Laser transport: stick a Laser Node on any chest, tank or machine. Click one node with a Laser Wrench, then another within 24 blocks in clear line of sight, to fire a laser between them (click both again to cut it). Open a node to set each channel (Items, Fluids, Energy) to Off, Send or Receive: senders push through every chain of linked nodes to receivers, highest priority first. Items can be filtered. Beams glow gold for items, blue for fluids and red for energy as they flow.
handbook.powerfactor.storage.title: Storage Network & Autocrafting
handbook.powerfactor.tesseract.text: Tesseracts on the same frequency are one block folded through space, in any dimension. Set each channel (items, fluids, energy) to Send or Receive. Push into a sending tesseract with pipes, cables or machines and it hands everything straight to the blocks touching the receiving ones, in the same transaction, so nothing is lost when they're full. Frequencies are private to you unless you unlock them. Tesseracts never feed each other, so frequencies can't loop. Both ends must be loaded (a Chunk Loader helps).
handbook.powerfactor.tesseract.title: Tesseract
handbook.powerfactor.time_field.text: The Time Dilation Field runs everything in its bubble faster: machines tick N times a tick and crops, saplings and cane grow N times as fast. Pick ×2, ×4, ×8 or ×16 on its console. Time is expensive: the field costs (N² − 1) × 40 FE/t, plus (N − 1)² × 8 FE/t for every machine inside, so ×16 with a room full of machines takes a fusion plant. Range Upgrades grow the bubble from 5 to 9 to 13 blocks across. Sneak past it at night to see its edges.
handbook.powerfactor.time_field.title: Time Dilation
handbook.powerfactor.title: PowerFactor
handbook.powerfactor.tools.text:
Electric Drill: pickaxe and shovel on FE. Sneak-use to install modules: 3x3 Area, Speed, Silk Touch, Fortune, Magnet, Battery.

Tesla Arc Gun: lightning that arcs between up to five targets.

Arc Saber: use to ignite, sneak-use to pick any RGB color, blade style (solid, plasma, crackling arc, rainbow) and hit effect (stun, ignite, chain arc, drain). Charge everything in a Charger.
handbook.powerfactor.tools.title: Tools and Weapons
handbook.powerfactor.transmission.text:
Low voltage loses a lot over distance. Step up.

Wire tiers: Copper Wire (512 CE), Insulated Cable (1,024), MV Aluminum Cable (4,096), and HV pylons (16,384) with far lower loss. Bare and insulated copper share 480 V and connect directly; a mixed run uses its weakest cable's rating. Different voltages need a transformer, including across closed breaker chains. Transformers join two grids: power enters the red primary face and leaves the blue secondary face, and they carry EE back upstream. Overload one and it trips; right-click to reset.

String HV conductors between pylons with a Conductor Spool, up to 32 blocks per span. Circuit Breakers split a grid when open and trip on overcurrent.
handbook.powerfactor.transmission.title: Transmission
handbook.powerfactor.turrets.text:
Turrets guard an area on FE. They engage hostile mobs by default. Animals and players are opt-in from the console. A turret never fires on whoever placed it, on villagers, on tamed pets or on armour stands, and it only shoots what it can see.

Plasma Turret: 20 m range, a bolt every 0.3 s at 1,500 FE each. Bolts burst without splash damage.

Railgun Turret: 40 m range. It charges for 1.5 s, then fires a slug that pierces every valid target along the line, for 40,000 FE a shot. Walls stop it.

The console's radar plots every creature in range, with hostiles in red. A redstone signal or SCADA can switch a turret off.

Shield Generator: projects a dome of force 4 to 16 m in radius. Hostile mobs inside are shoved back out, and projectiles fired by hostiles are burned away as they cross the surface. Upkeep is 3 FE/t per square metre of radius, plus 2,000 FE per repulse.
handbook.powerfactor.turrets.title: Defence Turrets
handbook.powerfactor.units.text:
PowerFactor measures three kinds of power.

FE (Forge Energy) is real power: it does the work, and every FE machine from any mod runs on it.

EE (Ender Energy) is reactive power. Motors need it to magnetize, but it does no work. It still has to be generated and carried.

CE (Creative Energy) is apparent power, the total the wires and generators actually see: CE = sqrt(FE^2 + EE^2).

Power factor is FE / CE. At 1.00 every bit of capacity does work.
handbook.powerfactor.units.title: FE, EE and CE
handbook.powerfactor.upgrades.text:
Upgrades go in the Upgrades tab.

Speed: +50% per card, but a bigger motor uses more FE and EE. Efficiency: -15% FE per job. Built-in Capacitor: cancels 5 EE of the machine's own motor each; three fix a stock crusher. VFD: the motor ignores frequency and voltage sag, uses a quarter of the EE and stops instead of idling. Surge Protector: rides through dips down to 0.6 pu. Capacity: a bigger FE buffer.

The Configuration tab sets redstone behavior, each face's role (input, output, both, closed) and auto-input and auto-eject.
handbook.powerfactor.upgrades.title: Upgrade Cards
handbook.powerfactor.upgrades_tools.text:
Put a Drill, Chainsaw, Jetpack, Arc Saber or Arc Gun in the middle of an Upgrade Table and fit up to six modules round it. Battery and Efficiency fit everything. Speed and Magnet suit the drill and chainsaw; Area, Silk Touch and Fortune the drill; Thruster and Plating the jetpack; Overcharge the blades and the gun; Chain Arc the saber and gun. Sockets light up for modules that fit. Modules travel inside the tool.

Wrench: turns machines, strips wire coating, and sneak-use dismantles any PowerFactor block into your inventory.
handbook.powerfactor.utility.text:
Chunk Loader: obsidian, gold and an eye of ender. It keeps the 3x3 chunks around it loaded and ticking. Right-click it with Range Upgrades to grow the area (up to three: 9x9); sneak-use with an empty hand to take one back. Sneak near it to see the loaded area.

Wireless Redstone: a powered Wireless Transmitter switches on every Wireless Receiver on its channel, in any dimension, while the transmitter is loaded. Use a dye on either to set its channel; the lamp shows it.

Item Magnet: use it to switch on. While on, anywhere in your inventory, it draws loose items and experience within 8 blocks to you, except items still under a pickup delay. Sneak to pause it.
handbook.powerfactor.utility.title: Handy Devices
handbook.powerfactor.vein.text: Combine any digging tool with a Vein Mining Matrix in an anvil (30 levels) and it learns vein mining. Hold the Vein Mine key (` by default) and the whole vein under your crosshair lights up. Break one block and the rest come away in a wave, up to 64 blocks within 16: every touching block of the same kind, or the same ore in other stone. Each costs the tool's durability or charge as if mined by hand, plus hunger, and it stops a block short of breaking the tool. The drops gather where you struck.
handbook.powerfactor.vein.title: Vein Mining
handbook.powerfactor.wire_safety.text: Bare wire on a live grid shocks whatever touches it: copper (480 V) stings, bare MV aluminium (13.8 kV) throws you back hard. Right-click a wire with Rubber to coat it; coated and insulated cable are safe to walk on. A wrench strips the coat off again. Mobs that wander onto bare live wire get the same treatment.
